facts.text: Roland Park was founded by Chicago firm Jarvis and Conklin in 1891, buying 500 acres near Lake Roland with $1M capital.
The neighborhood was the first Baltimore subdivision to use deed restrictions, setting covenants that barred businesses and required setbacks.
Frederick Law Olmsted Jr. and Edward Bouton designed the layout, with Olmsted Brothers laying out the second tract and installing graded streets and a Lake Roland Elevated Railroad.
Roland Park’s eclectic homes blend historic styles with Arts and Crafts, a hallmark of the area’s architectural character.
In 1974, Roland Park was added to the National Register of Historic Places, recognizing its status as a model streetcar suburb.
